references.text: Jacob named the place Bethel after his first encounter with God there. In 35:15 he repeats this naming after God spoke to him again at the same place.
Jacob builds an altar at Bethel and calls the place El-Bethel, because God revealed himself to him there. This is the immediate context for the naming in the following verse.
God identifies himself as 'the God of Bethel' and tells Jacob to return to his homeland, which directly links God's speech to the place Bethel.
Abraham builds an altar and calls on the name of the Lord at Bethel, showing the holy significance of the place already from the early history of the patriarchs.
Abraham returns to Bethel, the place where he first built an altar, demonstrating the enduring importance of the site in the patriarchal narratives.
God's command to go to Bethel (v.1) sets the context for the subsequent conversation and naming in v.15.
Hosea interprets Jacob's experience at Bethel as a permanent meeting place where God speaks to his people.
Jacob's vow to meet God at Bethel (v.3) is fulfilled through the conversation and naming in v.15.
